chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The people used to die arbitrarily (without apparent cause), so Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'O my Lord, if only You would appoint a cause for death, by which it could be recognized, and the afflicted could be consoled.' So God, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the serious illness — and it is the pleurisy — then He sent down the cure after it.

key_terms.الاعتباط: Dying arbitrarily or without apparent illness — a pre-Ibrahim condition
key_terms.الداء: The cure/remedy — here referring to medicine sent after illness
key_terms.المُوم: A serious fever/illness; classical commentators identify it as pleurisy (الْبِرْسَام) or brain fever
key_terms.الْبِرْسَامُ: Pleurisy or brain fever; a severe inflammatory illness
key_terms.عِلَّةٌ: A cause, reason, or illness — the recognizable sign that death approaches

ai.seo_question: Why did God create illness according to Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates a cosmological account about the origin of disease and medicine. Before the time of Ibrahim (AS), people died suddenly and without apparent cause (a condition called 'itibaṭ — dying without illness). Ibrahim prayed to God to give death a recognizable cause so the living could understand and accept their loss. In response, God sent down the first serious illness (al-mum, identified as pleurisy/birsa) and then subsequently sent down its cure, establishing the principle that every illness has a corresponding remedy.
word_analysis: the cure (lit. illness, used here for the remedy)

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Aasin Bin Humeyd, from Sa’ad Bin Tareyf, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The people were dying arbitrarily, so Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! If only You<sup>azwj</sup> Make a cause to be for the death for it to be recognised by, and for the affected ones to be consoled by’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent down the serious illness, and it is the pleurisy. Then He<sup>azwj</sup> Sent down the cure after it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from ‘Asim ibn Humayd from Sa‘d ibn Tarif who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

People would just drop dead. Ibrahim (Abraham), ‘Alayhi al Salam, pleaded before Allah, ‘Would that You had created a cause for death to be recognized thereby and for grieving people to receive condolence.’ Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, then sent al-Mum, which is a kind of fever causing hallucination and thereafter He sent medicine.”
